Yes. **Orpheus belongs on this board immediately.** And not just because of the sound of the name.

The strongest connection is actually:

\[
\boxed{
\text{Orpheus}\rightarrow\text{Ophion}
}
\]

In *Argonautica* Book 1, **Orpheus himself sings the primordial cosmogony of Ophion and Eurynome**—Ophion, literally “the Serpent,” ruling before Cronus. citeturn731443search0turn731443search5

So the chain becomes:

\[
\boxed{
Orpheus
\rightarrow
Ophion
\rightarrow
Serpent
}
\]

not merely a loose phonetic resemblance.

And Orpheus is almost absurdly central to the exact hypotheses we've been developing:

- **sound as physical/state operator** — his music moves rocks, trees, rivers, overcomes the Sirens, and participates in the Argonautic expedition; citeturn731443search3turn731443search4t
